reviewScope: All twelve graph/tree references and sixty actual language bodies, including full mutable random-node BST state APIs and uniform physical-node selection.

questions.algorithm: Build directed adjacency and explore reachable nodes with visited-at-enqueue flags and an indexed append-only queue.
questions.review: Read all five bodies. start==target is explicitly true before exploration. Edges are one-way; labels are distinct node IDs. Marking before queue append prevents cycles, self-loops and duplicate edges from repeated expansion. Python/JS adjacency rows are independent allocations, not shared repeated references. Queue head indices avoid front-removal shifts in every language. A separate repeated-edge-relaxation oracle checks all three-node directed graphs with every query pair and four-node graphs with a fixed endpoint pair, plus 1000-node chains, 10000 duplicate edges and random graphs. Boolean observations reject numeric substitutes. Original edge arrays/rows are unchanged.

questions.algorithm: Recursively choose a middle value of disjoint half-open sorted ranges, allocate one node and set each child Parent link.
questions.review: Read the author library constructor/parent setters and all five independently authored bodies. Recursion halves interval sizes and stays logarithmic for n<=1000. Input arrays remain unchanged and signed endpoints participate only in ordering/index lookup. The child observer serializes returned objects without computing an expected tree; host/C# graders independently check finite proper connectivity, exact parent links, inorder equality and the binary capacity minimum-height bound. Both two-element root choices are accepted. A compiled Python lower-midpoint alternative passes every minimal-tree case, proving reference shape is not a hidden requirement. C++ transfers new-node ownership and the private observer frees collected nodes after projection.

questions.algorithm: Build a fresh singly linked output list for each BFS frontier, storing original TreeNode references and enqueuing children left before right.
questions.review: Read all five actual bodies and supplied DepthLink APIs. New links have Value=the original node object; tree fields are never repurposed. A separate preorder-by-depth oracle produces original ID rows, including all small shapes, repeated Data, shuffled row IDs, selected internal roots, 1000-node chains and broad 1000-node trees. Private projection tracks output-link identities and bounds traversal so cycles/shared links cannot hang validation. Five compiled variants with equal-valued cloned Value nodes are rejected, and an actual linked-list cycle is rejected. C++ frees transferred output links only; input node ownership remains with the judge.

questions.algorithm: Explicit postorder enter/exit frames compute each node height once in an identity-keyed map.
questions.review: Read all five actual bodies. Children enter before parent exit, null heights are zero, and every node local difference is checked rather than only the root. The height map retains all processed entries, so the stated storage is O(n), not O(h). Java immutable frames, C# tuples, C++ value frames and Python/JS tuple arrays avoid recursive stack depth. An independent repeated level-height oracle checks all ordered shapes through seven nodes, selected internal subtrees and 1000-node skewed chains. Data is irrelevant and duplicate values do not merge node keys.

questions.algorithm: Iterative inherited lower-exclusive/upper-inclusive intervals enforce duplicate-left BST ordering at every depth.
questions.review: Read the public QuestionB condition and all actual language bounds. C#/Java/C++ use widened signed limits; Python exact integers and JS exact Number represent the below-minimum sentinel. No int endpoint +/-1 adjustment occurs. A separate descendant-value oracle checks every ancestor against every left/right descendant, including exhaustive short shapes/value assignments, signed endpoints and 1000-node duplicate chains. External Parent bounds do not affect a selected internal subtree. Language-specific WHY notes explain actual widening/representation choices.

questions.algorithm: Return the right-subtree leftmost original node, or climb Parent links past completed right-child subtrees.
questions.review: Read all five actual bodies. Comparisons use reference identity and never equal Data; null and final-node results are explicit. A separate complete-component inorder-ID oracle checks every selected node in all small ordered BST shapes, duplicate-left 1000-node chains and signed endpoints. The decoder passes actual provided TreeNode objects, and results are projected through private original-object IDs. Five compiled clone-return counterexamples yield unknown identity -2 despite equal Data; five parent-mutating examples return the correct original result but fail readonly snapshots.

questions.algorithm: Queue-based indegree elimination, returning the full project list or an empty result when not all projects can be emitted.
questions.review: Read every actual language body and the author nested EdgeRemoval source. A pair [before,after] increments after's indegree and appends after to before's adjacency. Repeated pairs are counted and decremented with the same multiplicity; a project enters only on its one transition to zero. Self-dependencies and cycles in a separate component cannot produce an accepted partial prefix. The grader accepts every valid permutation respecting all dependencies rather than requiring incidental queue order. Independent exhaustive permutations decide small-graph feasibility, with a heap/set oracle for large graphs. All four-node directed graphs, duplicate edges, no projects, 200-project chains/cycles and isolated nodes are executed.

questions.algorithm: Count Parent depths, align the deeper node, then advance original references together to their first meeting.
questions.review: Read the author parent-link variant and all actual bodies. Null inputs exit immediately, a node is its own ancestor, and two separate tree components converge only at null. No Data ordering is assumed. Python is, JS strict equality, C# ReferenceEquals and Java/C++ reference/pointer comparisons preserve identity. The independent oracle builds one ancestor-ID set and walks the second chain. All small-shape node pairs, same-valued nodes, disjoint components and 1000-node depth differences are executed. Auxiliary storage is constant.

questions.algorithm: Backtrack over the frontier of nodes whose parents are already chosen, exposing children only after selecting their parent.
questions.review: Read all five bodies. Each branch copies its available frontier, appends one distinct Data value, snapshots complete paths and pops afterward. No input TreeNode field is changed. Unique BST values make ancestor-before-descendant orders exactly insertion sequences; empty frontier emits one row, including [[]] for an empty tree. Independent exhaustive node-ID permutations filtered by original parent precedence establish expected sequences for all small shapes and selected eight-node cases. The grader sorts only outer row encodings, rejects duplicate rows and never sorts values inside a row. Actual frontier copying is included in the conservative O(S*(n+1)^2) bound.

questions.algorithm: Iterative null-aware preorder tokenization followed by whole-token KMP search.
questions.review: Read every actual token producer, prefix-table loop and search loop. Empty small returns true; explicit # markers and V-prefixed complete integer tokens distinguish shape and 2 from 12. Java uses a null-tolerant ArrayList traversal stack, C# nullable Stack, and other languages nullable pointer/list arrays. C# value formatting is invariant. All subtree comparisons ignore external Parent links while preserving them. A separate candidate-root/direct-structure-pair oracle checks every small tree pair, mirrored equal-value shapes, numeric boundaries and repeated-value 1000/500-node chains. Per-language WHY notes match actual containers and comparisons.

questions.algorithm: Iterative enter/exit events maintain frequencies only for ancestor-path prefix sums.
questions.review: Read all five bodies. Querying running-target occurs before inserting the current prefix, excluding empty paths. Exit events decrement the exact prefix and remove zero-frequency keys before a sibling is visited. Initial prefix zero remains once after traversal, and every method call owns a fresh map. Actual O(h) storage includes active frames/frequencies only. Independent enumeration from every start node covers exhaustive small signed-value shapes and targets, zero siblings, selected internal subtrees, a 1000-zero chain with 500500 nonempty paths and signed admitted bounds. No upward/cross-branch path is counted.

questions.algorithm: Maintain private subtree sizes on iterative BST insertion/deletion paths; select one uniform inorder rank and descend by left-subtree sizes.
questions.review: Read pinned Java Tree/TreeNode and author-linked JavaScript full API, then all five independent actual class bodies. Insert duplicates left; two-child deletion copies successor Data and removes exactly one successor, updating each retained ancestor once. The public invariant allows nondecreasing inorder because successor replacement can place equal values on the right. Query references are borrowed until mutation; no false node-stability guarantee is made across deletion. Private SizedNode subclasses carry counts, but the provided RandomNode API and grader do not require a cache layout. C++ deletes the physically removed node, frees all owned nodes iteratively at destruction and disables shallow copying. C#/Java cast only their own allocated subclasses; Python/JS store node objects and integer sizes. Reference operation complexity is O(h) worst case, not guaranteed logarithmic. Independent Counter semantics check every per-operation multiset delta and result, with exhaustive short update/query transcripts, signed endpoints, duplicates, successor cases and 1000-node skewed trees. Private readonly snapshots and identity maps reject cloned query nodes. Random choice is tested on physical-node inorder IDs lifted to permutations by uniformly ordering the complement, so equal Data cannot hide collapsed node identity. Exact small choice mass plus seeded sampling are finite regression checks, not a proof for arbitrary submissions; reference correctness follows the rank-node bijection. Five compiled breadth-first alternatives pass without using cached subtree sizes. Five collapsed-duplicate getters and five cloned-Find/no-op-Delete programs are rejected.

languageBindingReview.csharp: Read exact bool/int[] methods. List<int>[] adjacency rows are separately constructed, and List<int> queues use a growing head index. Readonly observation preserves original jagged-array row identities. BuildOrder returns a materialized array only after all projects have been emitted. TreeNode nullable fields are supplied before the solution. Enter/exit tuples carry explicit state; dictionary node keys identify objects. Node returns become original private IDs. All Data/Left/Right/Parent snapshots must remain unchanged. KMP uses nullable traversal entries and invariant integer tokens. Minimal construction uses a nullable local recursive helper and sets Parent on each fresh node. DepthLink heads are concrete List<DepthLink> values containing original nodes. Insertion paths/frontiers use independent List copies, including an empty path snapshot. RandomBst owns RandomNode objects and uses a private SizedNode subtype with subtree counts; readonly queries return current references and do not mutate Data or links. Iterative update paths prevent recursion overflow on 1000-node skewed trees. The random-node API is separate from the parent-linked TreeNode model.

Boolean results have exact boolean type; Number integer node IDs and degrees stay well below precision limits. Every returned order is a concrete array; input edges are not sorted or modified. Number bounds remain exact; Boolean/int results are checked separately. Parent alignment uses strict object equality. Fresh TreeNode/DepthLink constructors use the exact provided module classes. Depth lists retain original object references. Insertion frontiers use slice/concat and completed paths use slice so recursive mutation does not alias saved results. RandomBst owns RandomNode objects and uses a private SizedNode subtype with subtree counts; readonly queries return current references and do not mutate Data or links. Iterative update paths prevent recursion overflow on 1000-node skewed trees. The random-node API is separate from the parent-linked TreeNode model.

Reachability returns bool, which is validated separately from int. Build-order failure discards partial queue output. The observer maps id(node), not Data equality, and validates bool separately from int. Provided TreeNode annotations match the real user-module class. Explicit stacks support depth 1000; nullable entries are retained for structural KMP tokens. Snapshot checks also reject bool masquerading as Data int. A nested build helper creates fresh nodes and parent links. DepthLink.Value is the original object; projector identities are checked independently of Data. Frontiers and completed paths are copied, and all results are materialized lists. RandomBst owns RandomNode objects and uses a private SizedNode subtype with subtree counts; readonly queries return current references and do not mutate Data or links. Iterative update paths prevent recursion overflow on 1000-node skewed trees. The random-node API is separate from the parent-linked TreeNode model.

Dynamic queue growth does not invalidate iteration because the loop stores an index and adjacency traversal belongs to a different vector. Counts/IDs fit signed int; bounds are checked by input preconditions. TreeNode raw input pointers refer to judge-owned unique_ptr objects, whose addresses remain stable across vector growth. Solutions must not delete them. Pointer-key height maps, widened bounds and local value frames are explicit. Original-node returns are looked up by address, and every original field is resnapshotted. Returned minimal TreeNode and DepthLink objects are newly allocated and transferred to the private observer for cleanup. Depth Value pointers stay nonowning originals. Frontier vectors move into recursive calls, and result vectors copy the completed path before pop_back. RandomBst owns RandomNode objects and uses a private SizedNode subtype with subtree counts; readonly queries return current references and do not mutate Data or links. Iterative update paths prevent recursion overflow on 1000-node skewed trees. The random-node API is separate from the parent-linked TreeNode model.
languageBindingReview.java: Read actual methods, List<List<Integer>> adjacency and int[] result conversion. Boolean JSON encoding is explicit for reachability. Enhanced-for traverses adjacency lists while appending only to the separate queue, avoiding concurrent modification. Input row arrays remain unchanged. TreeNode fields/constructor are supplied, and the observer uses IdentityHashMap for original IDs. Traversal records never place null frames in ArrayDeque; KMP uses an ArrayList precisely because its stack contains null nodes. Boolean and Integer results have explicit JSON encoding. Local Search captures result/path lists and copies each completed sequence so later backtracking cannot erase it.
